subject: vue
question: What is the shorthand syntax for binding an attribute with the same name as a variable in Vue 3.4+, like :id="id"?
options: #id
@id
v-id
:id
explanation: Since Vue 3.4, :id with no value binds to a variable named id in scope.

subject: vue
question: Which syntax interpolates a value as text in a Vue template?
options: ${ message }
[[ message ]]
{{ message }}
<%= message %>
explanation: Vue uses double-curly mustache syntax for text interpolation, which is escaped as plain text.

subject: vue
question: What is the shorthand for v-bind:href?
options: @href
:href
#href
.href
explanation: A leading colon is the shorthand for v-bind.

subject: vue
question: Which directive provides an alternative block after a v-if when its condition is false?
options: v-otherwise
v-not
v-else
v-unless
explanation: v-else must immediately follow an element with v-if or v-else-if.

subject: vue
question: What is the shorthand for v-on:click?
options: :click
#click
$click
@click
explanation: The @ symbol is the shorthand for v-on event listeners.

subject: vue
question: Which directive renders an element only when an expression is truthy, removing it otherwise?
options: v-if
v-bind
v-show
v-model
explanation: v-if conditionally creates and destroys the element and its children.

subject: vue
question: Which function creates a Vue 3 application instance?
options: new Vue
Vue.mount
createApp
defineApp
explanation: Vue 3 apps start with createApp(App).mount('#app'), replacing the Vue 2 new Vue() constructor.

subject: vue
question: What does the v-html directive do?
options: Escapes the value and renders it as plain text
Loads markup from an external HTML file
Sets the element's innerHTML to the bound value
Validates HTML markup at compile time
explanation: v-html renders raw HTML via innerHTML, so it should never be used with untrusted content.

subject: vue
question: What does @keyup.enter="submit" do?
options: Calls submit on any key press
Prevents the Enter key's default action
Submits the parent form automatically
Calls submit only when the Enter key is released
explanation: Key modifiers filter keyboard events so the handler runs only for the named key.

subject: vue
question: What does @submit.prevent="onSubmit" do?
options: Prevents onSubmit from ever running
Stops event propagation but not the default
Calls event.preventDefault() and then runs onSubmit
Runs onSubmit only the first time
explanation: The .prevent modifier calls preventDefault() on the event before the handler runs.

subject: vue
question: What does :style="{ fontSize: size + 'px' }" do?
options: Creates a scoped style block
Adds a CSS class named fontSize
Binds an inline font-size style computed from size
Sets a style only on hover
explanation: Object syntax for :style accepts camelCase or quoted kebab-case CSS properties.

subject: vue
question: What does v-bind:[attrName]="url" do?
options: Binds an attribute whose name comes from the value of attrName
Binds an attribute literally named attrName
Binds every attribute listed in an array
Binds url only if attrName is true
explanation: Square brackets create a dynamic argument that is evaluated as a JavaScript expression.

subject: vue
question: Which of these is valid inside a mustache interpolation?
options: if (ok) { return 'YES' }
let label = 'YES'
ok ? 'YES' : 'NO'
for (const x of list) x
explanation: Template bindings accept a single JavaScript expression, not statements or declarations.

subject: vue
question: What does <div :class="{ active: isActive }"> render?
options: The class attribute is the literal object text
The active class is always added
It fails to compile because objects are not allowed
The active class is added only when isActive is truthy
explanation: Object syntax for :class toggles each class key based on the truthiness of its value.

subject: vue
question: What is the difference between @click="handle" and @click="handle()"?
options: The first passes the native event; the second calls it with no args
The first runs once; the second runs every click
They are identical and both receive the event
The first is invalid outside the Options API
explanation: A method name is called with the event, while an inline call uses only the arguments you write.

subject: vue
question: When using <template v-for> to render multiple elements per item in Vue 3, where should key go?
options: On each child element inside the template
On the template v-for tag itself
On the parent element around the loop
Nowhere, since keys are forbidden here
explanation: In Vue 3 the key belongs on the template tag rather than on its children.

subject: vue
question: In script setup, const obj = { id: ref(1) }. What does {{ obj.id + 1 }} render?
options: [object Object]1
NaN
explanation: Only top-level refs are unwrapped in templates, so obj.id is still a ref object inside the expression.

subject: vue
question: How is <MyComp v-bind="obj" title="x" /> resolved when obj also has a title property in Vue 3?
options: The v-bind object always wins
Individual attributes always win regardless of order
Order matters, and the later binding wins, so title="x" overrides obj.title
Vue throws a duplicate attribute error
explanation: Vue 3 merges bindings in the order they appear, unlike Vue 2 where individual attributes always won.

subject: vue
question: What is the result of v-on="{ mousedown: onDown, mouseup: onUp }" on an element?
options: Only the first listener is attached
A compile error, because v-on requires an argument
The object is passed as a single event name
Both listeners are attached, as object syntax binds multiple events
explanation: v-on without an argument accepts an object of event-to-handler pairs, but modifiers are not supported in that form.

subject: vue
question: A child root element has class="btn" and the parent renders it with class="large". What is the result?
options: The root element has only large
The root element has both btn and large
Vue warns and drops the parent class
The root element has only btn
explanation: class and style fall through and are merged with the classes already on the child's root.
